analysis:
The two units are documentation-only CHANGELOG.md text (head side, lines 1279-1852), with historical entries for v0.10.5 and earlier. They contain no executable code, so I found no concrete security regression. I checked the described behavior against the threat model.

SSD prefix cache (T-041). The entries on concurrent restores, mtime refresh, and eviction and maintenance (about 1618-1680) describe restores rewriting file mtime at most once per ttlSeconds/30, and TTL maintenance consulting the in-memory last-restore record. The text also says a restart can still drop such a file, and that disk-budget eviction orders by mtime. The 30-minute sliding TTL, the HMAC names, and the AAD and crypto bindings are said to be unchanged. A cached header (about 1654-1660) is remembered until the file changes. The text says the TTL, budget and ownership decisions are unchanged, but the implementation is not supplied, so I cannot verify it. Delta checkpoints (1733-1735) and the namespace bound to the binary and metallib hashes are consistent with T-041. The ssd-restore, header-cache and delta-checkpoint code is not in the supplied evidence.

Add-on hold (TB-012, T-059, T-060). The hardening entries (1802-1816) claim the signer is verified before a connection takes a slot, a 10-second request-line bound, non-blocking reads that refuse FIFOs, and a model-load fence. These match the T-059 and T-060 mitigations. The sandbox CLI entries (1537-1541) match the TB-013/T-061 scope. The installer fetched over HTTPS and run as the owner is previously documented as T-061, not new.

Release and signing. Entries at 1545-1565 are described as restricting dev builds to dev-branch pushes with Developer ID signing, notarization, and a designated-requirement check. This is consistent with T-034 and T-054 and weakens nothing, but the workflows themselves are not supplied.

Cluster, reconnect and App Attest. The 1590-1594 entry on reconnect backoff says registration and attestation are unchanged. The re-registration and Traffic status entries (1699-1731) say that only current evidence counts and that legacy verdicts count as authorized regardless of age. This relates to T-052, T-053 and T-057 and needs platform-side confirmation. Some HEAD entries in the cluster section are outside these units.

The remaining integration questions are source verification of these claims and the pair-update trust path in the part of the patch not supplied.
